1. Sitaram Khaitan, son of Sri Lal Khaitan 2. Shyam Bihari Khaitan, son of Sri Sitaram Khaitan  Both residents of Gherabari, P.S. Korha, District Katihar.

sentences.text:
.... .... Petitioners  Versus  The State Of Bihar  .... .... Opposite Party ===========================================================
Appearance :

For the Petitioners : Mr. N.K. Agrawal, Sr. Advocate  Mr. D.N. Tiwari, Advocate For the Opposite Party: Mr. Rajendra Prasad Nat, APP ===========================================================
CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE VIKASH JAIN ORAL JUDGMENT Date: 14-05-2015  Heard learned senior counsel for the petitioners and learned  APP for the State.

2. The present petition has been filed for quashing the  order dated 16.06.2011 passed by the learned Chief Judicial  Magistrate, Katihar taking cognizance in connection with B III Case  No.03 of 2011 for the offence under Sections 16 (1) (a) of the  Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (in short, "the Act").
 3.
Mr. N.K. Agrawal, learned senior counsel appearing on  behalf of the petitioners,

invites attention to the report of the Public  Analyst of the Combined Food & Drug Laboratory, Patna dated  08.01.2011 Sitaram Khaitan & Anr vs The State Of Bihar on 14 May, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173393102/
1 to show that apart from the presence of synthetic colouring matter, the sample of Masoor Dal does conform to the Patna High Court Cr.Misc. No.48446 of 2012 dt.14-05-2015 prescribed standard of quality in terms of the Act.

entities.text: Sitaram Khaitan & Anr vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that there is nothing in the said report to indicate that the colouring matter or any other ingredients was found to be of a nature injurious to health or otherwise unfit for human consumption.

Reliance was placed on various decisions of this Court in Cr. Misc. No.16358 of 2010 disposed of on 06.01.2011 (Awadh Bihari Lal Vs. The State of Bihar) and in Cr. Misc. No.16282 of 2012 disposed of on 03.08.2012 (Binod Kumar Agrawal Vs. The State of Bihar) including 2010 (3) PLJR 120 (Rajeev Kumar Vs. State of Bihar).
4. This Court finds considerable merit in the submissions advanced on behalf of the petitioner, and is of the view that mere presence of some colouring matter in the Masoor Dal which was not found to be injurious to health cannot justify the prosecution of the petitioner.
